flox-catalog.description: Versions the Flox catalog can actually resolve, unlike repology's nix_unstable which tracks nixpkgs directly and runs ahead of the flox/nixpkgs snapshots. Only versions built for every system in [options].systems are offered, so a bump cannot break the lock on one system.

flox-catalog-darwin.description: For packages the manifest restricts to aarch64-darwin (aerospace, maccy, container). The all-systems rule yields them zero releases, since they are macOS-only and never build for linux.

customManagers.description: Bump exact version pins resolved across every system in [options].systems. Requiring the pinned value to start with a digit skips the >= ranges (which float on their own) and the inline-table pins go/granted (deliberately held). This also matches the darwin-only packages, which the manager below claims as well; the duplicate is suppressed by the packageRule that disables this datasource for them. Renovate compiles custom-manager regexes with RE2, so a negative lookahead is not available to exclude them here.

Bump exact version pins for packages the manifest restricts to aarch64-darwin. Keep this name list in sync with the matchDepNames of the packageRule that disables the all-systems datasource for them, or a package will be offered two conflicting updates.
Bump zap flake ref to the latest tagged release

packageRules.description: Retained from the repology era so a failed flox-relock check still gets retried. The flox-catalog datasources only offer resolvable versions, so this should become unnecessary; drop it after a few clean runs.

Darwin-only packages are matched by both custom managers, since RE2 gives the all-systems manager no way to exclude them. Disabling the all-systems datasource for them leaves the flox-catalog-darwin result as the only update source.
aerospace has never cut a stable release; every catalog version is a -Beta prerelease. Without this Renovate finds no valid target and silently never opens a PR.
halloy versions are YYYY.M with an optional patch (2026.7, 2026.7.2), plus one legacy 23.1-alpha1. Not strict semver, but loose orders them correctly.

wezterm currently tags YYYY-MM-DD but the catalog still carries 12 legacy YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-hash versions. Under loose, 20240203 > 2026, so Renovate would propose a downgrade. This regex versioning matches only the current format, which makes the legacy versions invalid and therefore skipped.
